=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:15590-15598 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The Layer-2 branch re-resolution selects `ai:ready-to-merge` issues even though `detect_stalls` only consumes the re-anchored timestamp for `ai:done`, so the resolved value is never used.
  WHY: Reviewers consistently report that this turns each `ai:ready-to-merge` fallback lookup into dead `gh pr list` work with no effect on stall detection.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:15594-15598 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The Layer-2 jq filter does not handle unparseable non-empty `headPushedAt` values, so malformed timestamps do not trigger the branch-fallback path.
  WHY: Deepseek and moonshotai both note that the filter only gates on null/wrong-type/empty-string cases, while the wrapper logic was updated to fall back when a primary timestamp cannot be parsed.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:10476-10478,15598 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Layer-1 and Layer-2 can diverge on malformed `headPushedAt` handling, so different poll paths may anchor the same issue differently.
  WHY: x-ai reports an unparseable-but-non-empty `headPushedAt` stays on the primary path in Layer-1 while the Layer-2 re-anchor path can still be selected, which yields inconsistent stall decisions across ticks.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "Layer-2 branch fallback: before invoking the detector, the bash prefetch step re-resolves the `ai/issue-<n>` head branch ... for any `ai:done` / `ai:ready-to-merge` wave issue whose cross-reference produced no `headPushedAt`"
  expected_change_site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh or scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:_PHASES_WITH_PUSH_REANCHOR
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  EVIDENCE: `_PHASES_WITH_PUSH_REANCHOR = frozenset({"ai:done"})` at `orchestrate_lib.py:1783` contains only `ai:done`, the shell filter at `orchestrate_poll_process.sh:15598` selects both phases, the test at `tests/test_stall_freshness_branch_fallback.py:406/420` expects issue 102 (`ai:ready-to-merge`) to be selected, and the README text remains contradictory about whether both phases are re-anchored.
- requirement: "Layer 1 — `_check_fresh_push_guard_with_fallback` wraps the guard at both call sites; on a cross-ref cache-miss for `ai:done`/`ai:ready-to-merge` it re-checks freshness from the branch-resolved head commit before dispatching a recovery."
  expected_change_site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh around line 15595
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  EVIDENCE: The Layer-1 wrapper at line ~10476 now parses the primary timestamp with `date -d` and only skips the branch lookup when it is genuinely parseable, but the Layer-2 jq filter at line ~15594 checks only `null`, wrong type, or empty string and does not detect unparseable non-empty strings; no diff hunk adds that parity.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 15590-15598, the jq selection filter `any(. == "ai:done" or . == "ai:ready-to-merge")`
  Problem: The Layer-2 re-anchor fallback resolves branch-based head-commit timestamps for `ai:ready-to-merge` issues, but `detect_stalls` only consumes the map for `ai:done`, so the resolved timestamp is never used.
  Why it fails at runtime: Each `ai:ready-to-merge` wave issue missing a cross-ref `headPushedAt` incurs one wasted `gh pr list --head ai/issue-N --json number,commits` REST call per poll tick.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 15590-15598, the jq selection filter's non-string type check `((.value.linked_pr.headPushedAt | type) != "string")`
  Problem: The Layer-2 selection filter does not select issues whose primary `headPushedAt` is an unparseable non-empty string (e.g., `"not-a-timestamp"`). These pass through the filter unchanged.
  Why it fails at runtime: The Layer-1 wrapper (`_check_fresh_push_guard_with_fallback`) was fixed in the last-run diff to detect and fall back on unparseable primary timestamps, but the Layer-2 code path was not updated to match.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- Requirement: PR description states "Layer-2 branch fallback: before invoking the detector, the bash prefetch step re-resolves the `ai/issue-<n>` head branch ... for any `ai:done` / `ai:ready-to-merge` wave issue whose cross-reference produced no `headPushedAt`" — implying the resolved timestamps should affect stall detection for both phases.
  Expected change site: Either `scripts/orchestrate_lib.py` to expand `_PHASES_WITH_PUSH_REANCHOR` to `frozenset({"ai:done", "ai:ready-to-merge"})`, or `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` to narrow the jq filter to `. == "ai:done"` only, plus `tests/test_stall_freshness_branch_fallback.py` test expectation update, plus README consistency fix.
  Evidence of absence: `_PHASES_WITH_PUSH_REANCHOR = frozenset({"ai:done"})` at `orchestrate_lib.py:1783` contains only `ai:done`. The shell filter at `orchestrate_poll_process.sh:15598` selects both phases. The test at `test_stall_freshness_branch_fallback.py:420` expects issue 102 (label `ai:ready-to-merge`) to be selected. The README at line 1303 documents the fallback for both phases while line 1299 says "only `ai:done` is re-anchored." No diff hunk in this PR reconciles these contradictions.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- Requirement: PR description says "Layer 1 — `_check_fresh_push_guard_with_fallback` wraps the guard at both call sites; on a cross-ref cache-miss for `ai:done`/`ai:ready-to-merge` it re-checks freshness from the branch-resolved head commit before dispatching a recovery." — the wrapper was updated in the LAST RUN DIFF to handle unparseable primary timestamps (checking `date -d` parseability before skipping the branch fallback). The Layer-2 shell code should mirror this logic but does not.
  Expected change site: The Layer-2 jq filter in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` around line 15595 should also select issues whose `headPushedAt` is present but unparseable, matching the Layer-1 fix already applied in `_check_fresh_push_guard_with_fallback`.
  Evidence of absence: The Layer-1 wrapper at line ~10476 now parses the primary timestamp with `date -d` and only skips the branch lookup when it is genuinely parseable. The Layer-2 jq filter at line ~15594 checks only `null`, wrong type, or empty string — it does not detect unparseable non-empty strings. The last-run diff does not contain any hunk that adds unparseable-timestamp detection to the Layer-2 filter.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line: ~15597
  Problem: The Layer-2 jq selection filter selects both `ai:done` AND `ai:ready-to-merge` issues for branch re-resolution, but `detect_stalls` in `orchestrate_lib.py` only consumes `--head-pushed-at-json` for phases in `_PHASES_WITH_PUSH_REANCHOR = frozenset({"ai:done"})`.
  Why it fails at runtime: This means every `ai:ready-to-merge` issue missing a cross-ref `headPushedAt` incurs one unnecessary `gh pr list --head ai/issue-N --json number,commits` REST call whose returned timestamp is merged into `_head_pushed_at_json` but never consumed by `detect_stalls`.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- Requirement: From README.md line ~1303 — "Scope is intentionally narrow — only `ai:done` is re-anchored. Other phases retain their existing `status_since_ts`-only semantics."
  Expected change site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh - the jq filter that selects issues for Layer-2 branch re-resolution should match `_PHASES_WITH_PUSH_REANCHOR` in orchestrate_lib.py
  Evidence of absence: The jq filter at line ~15597 includes `ai:ready-to-merge` in the selection (`any(. == "ai:done" or . == "ai:ready-to-merge")`), but `_PHASES_WITH_PUSH_REANCHOR` in orchestrate_lib.py:1783 only contains `ai:done`. The test at tests/test_stall_freshness_branch_fallback.py:420 also expects issue 102 (`ai:ready-to-merge`) to be selected. The README Layer-2 section contradicts itself - first stating "only ai:done is re-anchored" then documenting the fallback runs for "ai:done / ai:ready-to-merge" wave issues.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

  Why it fails at runtime: An unparseable timestamp string is still a string type in jq, so it passes the type check but fails later parsing. These issues won't get the branch fallback even though they should.
